discovery: Prediction and discovery of flat bands, correlated insulators and superconductivity in magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene

nominees.name: Allan H. MacDonald
nominees.affiliation: University of Texas at Austin, USA

subfield: Condensed matter physics: 2D materials and moire quantum matter
motivation: In 2011 Bistritzer and MacDonald introduced a continuum theory of twisted bilayer graphene predicting that, at specific 'magic' twist angles near 1.1 degrees, the Dirac velocity vanishes and electronic bands become nearly flat, so electron-electron interactions dominate. In 2018 Jarillo-Herrero's group realised this prediction experimentally, discovering correlated insulating states and unconventional superconductivity in magic-angle graphene. Together these works created 'twistronics': the twist angle became a new, continuously tunable knob that turns a simple carbon sheet into a platform for strongly correlated physics. The field has since revealed orbital ferromagnetism, the quantum anomalous Hall effect, Chern insulators and, in related moire materials, fractional quantum anomalous Hall states at zero magnetic field. This is a rare example of a clean, quantitative theoretical prediction followed by a decisive experiment that opened an entire research area in quantum materials.
